core_obligations: Build the flat base change B' = A' tensor_A B, index the maximal ideals m'_{j,l} of B' over the maximal ideals m_j of B, and read off the factorization of a_1 and a_2 in each B'_{j,l} from the given factorization in B_j (chow.tex lines 1031-1050).

Reduce the comparison of the two displayed products to the single displayed identity of lines 1055-1061: for every unit u of B_j, the m-th power of Norm_{kappa_j/kappa}(u mod m_j)^{m_j} equals the product over l of Norm_{kappa'_{j,l}/kappa'}(u mod m'_{j,l})^{m'_{j,l}}.

Prove that identity by rewriting both sides as determinants of the same finite-length module: identify Norm(u)^{m_j} with det_kappa(u : M to M) for M = B_j/pi_j B_j, apply flat base change of determinants to get det_{kappa'}(u : M tensor_A A' to M tensor_A A'), and use the direct-sum decomposition M tensor_A A' = direct sum_l B'_{j,l}/pi_j B'_{j,l} together with multiplicativity of determinants in short exact sequences.

proof_roadmap.step: Dispose of the case where a_1 and a_2 are units, then choose A contained in B with local factorizations and write out both sides by definition (lines 1011-1028).

proof_roadmap.step: Form B' = A' tensor_A B using flatness, index its maximal ideals over those of B, and write partial_{A'} through the induced factorizations (lines 1030-1050).

spans.label: flat base change of the factorization data

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the displayed norm identity for one unit and prove it by determinants, flat base change of determinants, and the decomposition of M tensor_A A' (lines 1052-1085).

difficulty_reason: The statement compares two elements living in different residue fields: partial_A(a_1,a_2) raised to m = length_{A'}(A'/mA') in kappa must map to partial_{A'}(a_1,a_2) in kappa' for a flat local homomorphism A to A' of 1-dimensional Noetherian local rings. The proof at chow.tex lines 1031-1050 must first transport the factorization data along the flat base change B' = A' tensor_A B and index the maximal ideals of B' over those of B, which is what makes the two displayed products comparable at all. The remaining work is the single displayed identity of lines 1055-1061, proved by identifying the norm power with det_kappa(u : B_j/pi_j B_j to itself), applying flat base change of determinants and then splitting the base-changed module over the maximal ideals of B' (lines 1062-1085); the exponent m = length_{A'}(A'/mA') is exactly what makes the two determinant expressions match.
